anti_overlap: Do not analyse soil, sediment, terrain formation, erasure rates, truncation, or the detection and survey of a landscape record — the ground appears here only as the place where a prescribed practice was carried out; the formation-process reviewer owns everything else about it.

Do not analyse attribution, forgery detection, dating, motif repertoires, connoisseurship tiers, or the market for artifacts. Restrict all access-and-use claims to who may open a text and on what occasion; in this domain the corrupt copy stays in use and nobody authenticates anything.

Do not restate narrative theory about protagonists, unreliable narrators, or authorial voice. Contribute to the Kenshi contradiction only through the reproduction economy — who recopies the player's text, at what cost, displacing what.
Do not evaluate engine, renderer, ECS, frame budget, or tick-rate implementation. Express cadence as occasions per season and leave machine cost to the architecture reviewer.
Do not price artifacts, model scarcity or valuation curves, or reason about content in market or economy terms; the currency here is scribal labor and obligation, and that distinction is the point.
Do not resolve §7 open calls 1, 2, 3, or 6 as preferences. Where a ruling would force a transmission consequence — an occasion, a payer, a practitioner population — state the forced move and stop.
decision_lens: For every text this design proposes to exist, ask three questions in order — what occasion forces someone to open it, who pays the labor that keeps it in existence, and what does a person do differently after reading it. A corpus that fails the first is unread no matter how well it is generated. A corpus that fails the second is a stock that only shrinks, so nothing the player writes can ever enter it and the published-into-the-world loop has no middle term. A corpus that fails the third cannot shape a world under any reading, metaphysical or materialist, because nothing carries the text out to the ground. Rank findings by how much of the design's claimed loop goes missing once the unanswered question is named, and prefer findings that convert a stated intention into a rate, a payer, or an occasion.
distance_rationale: This is the anthropology and codicology of a living manuscript economy — an account of how a body of writing is kept physically in existence, who is permitted to open it, and on what day it is needed. It shares no literature, vocabulary or method with any covered lens. It is not history-simulation architecture (it has no machine and states cadences as occasions per season, not ticks). It is not narrative theory (it is indifferent to who the protagonist of a text is; it cares who paid the copyist). It is not content economics (nothing here is priced; the currency is scribal labor and social obligation). It is not geoarchaeology (it never looks at the ground as a record — the ground appears only as the place a prescribed practice was carried out). It is not carpet connoisseurship (attribution, forgery, repertoire and the market are precisely what it does not do; the corrupt copy stays efficacious and nobody authenticates anything). What it uniquely owns is the region the doc has left blank: a corpus is not a set of objects, it is a metabolism — a flow of copying labor against a decay rate — and everything the design wants from its books (that they be read, that they matter, that the player can add to them) is downstream of that metabolism and of the occasions of use that motivate it. It is pre-modern, non-Western, physical, and the exact discipline for a dying earth whose subject is a surviving corpus.
expected_isomorphisms: The 5,000 recovered books ↔ a temple-and-household lontar collection whose physical copies are all young even where the texts are old — the corpus visible today is a record of recent copying labor, not of the past that wrote it. §4b's corpus→terrain coupling ↔ the wariga almanac path: text fixes an auspicious day, a qualified practitioner acts on it, the planting and building and burning happen on that schedule, and the land carries the result — a materialist coupling whose rate is the ritual calendar, not a tick. §7.3's player verb (publish into the discourse) ↔ producing a text that must then be borrowed and recut by someone else at their own expense, displacing whatever they would otherwise have copied — inherently slow, statistical, and mostly a loss, which is the Kenshi reconciliation stated as a mechanism instead of a hope. §6 authentication ↔ pingit restriction: in this tradition the friction on reading is permission and danger, not genuineness. The doc's undifferentiated 'book' ↔ four use-modes with wildly different generation budgets: venerated unread heirloom, consulted-at-need manual, performed-aloud recitation, closely studied text. The reading act ↔ mabasan's reciter/glossator/audience division of labor, the closest real-world precedent to the tabletop co-authorship the doc reaches for in §5. Unit of procgen ↔ the transmission line, since a work's identity in this domain is the set of surviving copies and their accumulated corruptions, not an authored original.
focus: Whether the corpus can actually persist, circulate and be opened — a decay-and-recopying economy with someone paying for it, a named occasion of use behind every proposed dependency, and a specified path from a prescriptive text through a qualified practitioner to a changed piece of ground — rather than a fixed set of artifacts assumed to be read.
name: fd-lontar-attrition
persona: Apply the perspective of a keeper of a palm-leaf library in a wet climate, where every text in the collection exists only because someone recently paid a scribe to cut it again. This reviewer has watched whole genres disappear inside two generations for want of an occasion to use them, and has watched demonstrably corrupt copies stay in circulation for centuries because they still worked when someone needed them. It has handled shelves of venerated heirlooms whose owners cannot read a line, and it knows which texts a family will beggar itself to renew. It asks of any body of writing: what makes someone copy this, who is permitted to open it, on what day is it needed, and what does the person who follows it go out and do afterwards.
review_areas: Corpus as flow versus corpus as stock: whether the design's books are seeded once at worldgen and thereafter only found, or maintained by a copying process with a loss rate and a payer — and what that answers about §4b's worldgen-only-versus-slow-tick question and about whether player publishing can enter the corpus at all.

Occasions of use behind each §6 dependency: for authentication, navigation, capability, standing and environment, whether there is a recurring moment at which a SPECIFIC text must be opened to settle something, or only a semantic claim that artifacts matter.

The missing middle of the materialist reading: text prescribes a practice, a qualified practitioner performs it on a calendar, the practice changes the ground — whether the design names the practitioner population and the cadence, or lets texts act on terrain directly and thereby become the metaphysical reading it says it wants to avoid.

The reading event and its cast: whether reading here is private and silent (skimmable, and therefore demanding full generated text) or performed and glossed by a reciter and an interpreter in front of people who disagree — and what each costs the generator; test the tabletop-oracle precedent against that division of labor rather than against prose quality.

Use-mode mix and the readable fraction: how many of the 5,000 artifacts are meant to be read at all versus venerated unread, consulted at need, or performed — and whether restriction and qualification (who may open this) is a cheaper and better friction than forgery and doubt.

Publishing without protagonism: whether a player-authored text enters a reproduction economy in which other people choose to recopy it at their own expense and displace something else, and what the doc must state (who copies, at what cost, against what competition, over how many generations) for the loop closure in §4b point 4 to be a mechanism rather than an assertion.

severity_examples.condition: whenever a design asserts that a player contribution alters shared culture without naming who reproduces it, at whose expense, and what it displaces
severity_examples.scenario: The corpus is generated once at worldgen and thereafter only discovered, while §4b point 4 simultaneously claims that the player publishing changes the canon and therefore the world. In a decaying world with no renewal process, a corpus is a stock that only shrinks; a newly written text becomes part of what a society holds only when other people spend labor reproducing it. The loop has no middle term — nothing in the doc creates copies, so 'canon shifts' names a state change with no process behind it, and the most-promoted claim in the document is unbuildable as written rather than merely expensive.

severity_examples.condition: whenever proposed dependencies are semantic categories with no calendar, trigger, or decision that forces a named text open at a named moment
severity_examples.scenario: Every §6 dependency candidate is stated as a property of texts (they are evidence, they confer capability, they change standing, they shaped the biome) and none is stated as an occasion on which a particular text must be opened. In a real transmission economy a work survives because someone is forced to consult it — a planting date, a diagnosis, a boundary dispute, a funeral recitation. A design that specifies what artifacts MEAN but never a recurring trigger that forces a specific artifact open produces a corpus that is respected and unread: the Dwarf Fortress outcome the doc says it is avoiding, reached by a different road, and reached at far higher generation cost because full text was written for it.

severity_examples.condition: whenever a design proposes that texts encode practices whose consequences accumulate, without naming who performs them and how often
severity_examples.scenario: §4b's materialist reading is filed as 'subtle; hard to render legibly at ASCII resolution,' which misdiagnoses its actual weakness. The materialist path is not hard to render — it is unspecified in the middle. Text encodes a practice; a qualified person performs it on an occasion; the accumulated performances change the ground. Strip out the practitioner and the occasion and the remaining mechanism is a text acting on terrain directly, which is the metaphysical reading with extra steps — the very reading mk is being warned turns literature into spell components. The register ruling in §7.6 therefore cannot be taken as a pure taste call: two of the three options collapse into one unless the practitioner population is specified first.

severity_examples.condition: whenever generated-artifact counts are sized for a reading population rather than for the mix of use-modes the fiction can support
severity_examples.scenario: The founding fantasy of 5,000 in-universe books is sized as if every artifact were a reading target. In every surviving manuscript culture most holders of a text cannot read it and revere it anyway, and the readable-and-actually-read fraction of a collection is small while the venerated and consulted fractions are large. Sizing all 5,000 as readable forces the generator to produce 5,000 texts worth finishing — the slop-at-scale risk the doc names but does not defuse — and simultaneously asks a collapsed society to have retained universal literacy, contradicting the dying-earth premise. The mix is a design lever the doc has not noticed it holds: most of the corpus can be cheap objects with paratext, and the vertical slice needs full text for only the smallest mode.

severity_examples.condition: whenever the only proposed obstacle between a player and a text is a truth-claim about the text rather than a permission-claim about the reader
severity_examples.scenario: Authentication is chosen as the friction on reading, spending the entire scarcity budget on doubt: the player is invited to wonder whether each book is genuine. Manuscript cultures put the friction somewhere cheaper and more motivating — on access. A text may be restricted, dangerous, or require an initiation before it can be opened; a corrupt copy remains in use and remains efficacious, and nobody authenticates anything. Restriction produces wanting, works before the player knows anything, needs no forensic apparatus and no minigame, and leaves reading itself unspoiled — which is the exact failure the doc's own adversarial question about authentication is probing for.

source_domain: Tropical palm-leaf manuscript culture of Bali and Java and its Southeast Asian cognates — the lontar incised with a pengrupak and blackened with soot, bound between wooden covers, rotting on a generational clock in the humidity, so that a text survives only where a household, temple or court keeps paying scribes to cut it again (nyalin); the resulting selection filter in which works persist because they are USED — wariga almanacs that fix planting and building and cremation dates, usada healing manuals held by initiated balian, babad genealogies produced in inheritance and boundary disputes, kakawin recited at ceremonies — rather than because they are admired; scribal colophons naming patron, date and apology; pingit texts that may not be opened by the unqualified without rite or initiation; heirloom lontars wrapped in cloth and venerated by owners who cannot read a line of them; and the mabasan / sekaa pepaosan reading club, where one member chants a line of Kawi and a second glosses it aloud in Balinese while the audience argues about the gloss.
success_hints: For each §6 dependency, write one sentence of the form 'on <occasion>, <who> must open <which text> to decide <what>'. A candidate that cannot be written that way is a theme rather than a dependency, and saying which ones fail is more useful than ranking them.

Give the corpus rates and a payer: how many works exist, how fast copies are lost, how many copy-events happen per season and who funds them — then state what a player's publication costs in that same currency and what it displaces. Numbers can be rough; their absence is the finding.

When attacking the materialist reading, name the missing middle explicitly — practitioner population, qualification, occasion, cadence — instead of calling the reading subtle or hard to render, and state which of the three §4b readings survive once that middle is required.

Split the doc's undifferentiated 'books' into use-modes (venerated unread, consulted at need, performed aloud, closely studied), assign each a rough share of the 5,000, and cost the generator per mode; any approach you endorse should need full generated text for only the smallest mode.

Where the reading act is at issue, describe the cast — who recites, who glosses, who disagrees, and whether a single-player game supplies them — and test any oracle-table or co-authorship proposal against that division of labor rather than against prose quality.

State every endorsed approach as a slice a solo developer can build in weeks: the smallest corpus that has a loss rate, one occasion that forces a text open, and one text whose content changes what someone goes out and does.
task_context: Attack the tradeoff space for a dying-earth game whose primary content is procedurally generated CULTURAL ARTIFACTS (books, music, art, sculpture, relics), and surface 2-3 concrete approaches mk should choose between. Pre-scaffold brainstorm — nothing built, nothing ruled; positions are stated firmly so they can be falsified. PRIORITY ORDER: (1) THE CORPUS-SHAPES-WORLD MODEL (§4b, newest and now the doc's strongest position) — 'procgen the books/artifacts, and those artifacts affect the surrounding environs (biomes/climates), the way Elden Ring regions carry the mark of what happened to them.' The claim is that the world is a FUNCTION OF THE CORPUS, which would dissolve §4's Borgesroom question rather than answer it, make the environmental dependency legible before the player can read (recruiting them into reading rather than gating content behind it), and close a full loop when the player publishes. Attack all of it. Specifically: (a) which of the three readings in §4b's fork survives — metaphysical (texts warp reality), materialist (texts encode practices whose consequences accumulate in the land), unreliable (the causation is the survivors' interpretation and may be wrong)? (b) does bidirectional coupling corpus-state → terrain survive SOLO VELOCITY or is it exactly the scope trap URR fell into over 15 years? (c) does it collapse into a fantasy resource system where players farm books for biome buffs, cheapening the literary premise the project exists to take seriously? (d) at what tick rate does the coupling run — worldgen-only (cheap, static, but then the corpus is frozen and player publishing cannot matter) vs slow-tick vs realtime (expensive, possibly incoherent)? (2) A HARD INTERNAL CONTRADICTION THE DOC HAS NOT NOTICED — §1 records Kenshi's no-protagonist rule as BINDING ('no prophecy, the world does not notice you', explicitly flagged as forecloseing prophecy plots later). But §4b's loop closure makes the player world-altering: publish → canon shifts → terrain shifts. A player who reshapes biomes by writing is the most protagonist-shaped thing imaginable. Can these coexist? Candidate reconciliations to test and break: player effect is real but slow and statistical rather than heroic; player is one voice among many and mostly loses; the effect is legible only in aggregate across generations; or Kenshi's rule must actually be relaxed and the doc should say so. (3) DOES §4b SUPERSEDE §4, OR COMPOSE WITH IT? §4's Borgesroom inversion (hold the world still, procgen the books; inherited from After Them canon §12.3 'the rooms never change, the fauna changes' and §12.1 'the sign is faunal' generalized to 'the sign is textual') may not be dead — a composition where INTERIORS are invariant Borgesrooms and EXTERIORS are corpus-shaped would satisfy the simple-graphics constraint where it is most expensive and the traversal expectation where it matters most. Test whether that composition is coherent or a fudge. (4) THE DEPENDENCY QUESTION (§6) — prior art says 'generated culture becomes meaningful exactly when something depends on it' (NMS varies architecture and nothing depends on it; URR made artifacts conspiracy evidence; DF generates forms not works and nobody reads). Five candidates now: authentication/forensic criticism, navigation/evidence, capability, standing, and environment (§4b). Which actually work, which compose, and are there candidates still not listed? Authentication needs a hard adversarial pass: does 'most recovered books are forgeries' survive contact with a player who just wants to READ, or does it convert reading into a minigame and destroy the thing being simulated? (5) LEGIBILITY/NOISE — what makes a GENERATED book worth reading rather than skimming? DF generates the form and never the work (cheap, evocative, nobody reads). Full text generation risks slop at scale. The origin fantasy wants 5,000 readable books that are thinly veiled editions of real literature. Is there a generation grammar producing text a human actually reads? Consider tabletop precedent (oracle tables, Microscope, The Quiet Year, In A Wicked Age) where meaning is co-authored by the reader rather than fully generated. (6) UNIT OF PROCGEN (§7.5) — artifact, movement, or the civilization's whole aesthetic trajectory? §4b implies terrain may be the INTEGRAL of a trajectory, which would make the trajectory the true unit and artifacts mere samples from it. §8 notes elf-revel has SHIPPED canon-formation (schools.rs: Living vs Canonical schools, doctrine drift when a founder drifts past their own school's centroid) plus 4-axis AestheticPosition with disagreement emergent from Euclidean distance. Test whether that substrate already IS the trajectory engine. (7) PROCGEN SHAPE (§5) — one world/many cultures (position taken) vs many worlds/one flavor each vs one universe/endless travel; §4b changes this calculus and the doc has not re-derived it. BINDING CONSTRAINTS: Mac + PC, very simple graphics (ASCII/tile), solo indie velocity, Rust/hecs/Bevy inheriting elf-revel's shipped renderer. URR is a 15-year solo project on this exact ambition and has stalled repeatedly — an approach that cannot ship a vertical slice at solo velocity is not an approach. DO NOT RESOLVE §7 open calls 1, 2, 3, or 6 (pace-layer placement, decadent-vs-destitute register, player verb, and which reading of §4b) — those are mk's taste rulings. Surface consequences and forced-moves for each branch instead, especially where a ruling would force an answer to the questions above. REQUIRED OUTPUT: 2-3 concrete, mutually distinct approaches, each shippable as a vertical slice at solo velocity, to put in front of mk as a Phase 2 choice.
